chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Fadhl said:

Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) regarding Ibn Asbat, saying to him: 'What do you think regarding him, while Ibn Asbat is present, and we are all traveling by sea or by land to Egypt?' And he informed him of the news of the land route. He (the Imam) said: 'Go to the mosque at a time other than that of an obligatory prayer, and pray two rak'ahs, and seek God's guidance (istikhara) one hundred times. Then see what comes to your heart, and act upon it.' And Ibn al-Jahm said to him: 'The land route is more preferable to me.' He (the Imam) said: 'And to me as well.'
ai.seo_question: How to perform the Istikhara prayer for choosing between two permissible options?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the Prayer of the Compelled (*Salat al-Mudtir*), this narration highlights the practical application of Istikhara for choosing between two valid alternatives rather than general decision-making. Imam al-Rida (AS) specifies performing two units in the mosque outside of obligatory times, emphasizing that the subsequent heart inclination (*ma yaqulu qalbuka*) serves as the divine indicator for action. This method underscores the Shia scholarly view that Istikhara is a spiritual discipline to align one’s will with God’s wisdom when faced with permissible choices.
